lines.text: You'd never lose forty days of sleep over one parking spot.
These three neighbours did.
Their tech park has exactly one bay in the shade.
Day one. Rohan leaves at eight thirty. Gone.
Day five. Priya leaves at eight. Gone.
Day twelve. Arjun leaves at seven. Still gone.
Day thirty. Rohan stops going home and just sleeps in the car park.
Day forty. All three pull in at six a.m., ready for war.
And the bay is already taken.
By a hatchback with four strangers inside, eating breakfast.
Then they finally read the sign.
Carpools only.
It said that on day one too.
So they agree to share. One rule: whoever wakes up first drives.
Next morning, three alarms at five. Three drivers. Three cars at the gate.
Again.
Turns out a parking war is just a carpool nobody organised.
So now an app runs the roster and says whose turn it is.
No alarms. No racing. Can't come? Hit skip today.
Day sixty. One car, three friends, the shady bay, every morning.
Rohan still sleeps in the car, though. Just in the back seat now.
If your commute feels like a race, try Sahyatri.
